Testimony of Representative Holly Eaton introducing
LD 2234, An Act to Increase the Debt Limit of the Vinalhaven Water District
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities and Technology

Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs and members of the Energy, Utilities and Technology
Committee, my name is Holly Eaton, and I represent House District 15, which includes the
working waterfronts and island communities of Deer Isle, Stonington, Brooklin, Tremont,
Southwest Harbor, Frenchboro, Swan's Island, Isle au Haut and Vinalhaven. I am pleased to be
before you today to introduce LD 2234, Am Act to Increase the Debt Limit of the Vinalhaven
Water District.
This legislation increases the borrowing authority of the Vinalhaven Water District from $1.5 million to $4 million. They are seeking this increase so that the district can complete necessary
infrastructure improvements, including the installation of a new water main and a mitigation
project needed to bring the system into compliance with state standards. These improvements are essential to protecting public health and ensuring reliable water service for the residents of Vinalhaven.
Following my testimony, representatives from the Vinalhaven Water District will testify over zoom and are prepared to answer any technical or proj ect-specific questions the committee may
have.
I also want to take a moment and thank the committee for its willingness to hear this bill after the filing deadline. The needs of this water system are immediate, and I appreciate your
consideration so that my constituents can receive the support they need in a timely mamier.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Testimony of Island Institute in Support of LD 2234, An Act to Increase the Debt Limit of the Vinalhaven Water District March 19, 2026
Senator Lawerance, Representative Sachs, and Members of the Energy, Utilities, and Technology Committee, my name is Nick Battista, and I am testifying on behalf of Island Institute in support of LD 2234.
Island Institute is a 42-year-old nonprofit organization based in Rockland, Maine. We boldly navigate climate and economic change with island and coastal communities to expand opportunities and deliver solutions. Much of our work takes place in the communities that are highly dependent on fishing, and the bulk of these communities are east of Damariscotta.
Some of these communities have public water infrastructure and one of these communities, Vinalhaven, needs support in the form of lifting its debt limit to make some much needed upgrades. The current debt limit for the water district was set at $1.5m in 1978 and hasn't changed since. If that had been indexed to inflation, the water district today would have had the power to borrow about $7.4m. The water district is only looking for an increase of $2.5m, for a total borrowing power of $4m.
The upgrades contemplated by Vinalhaven water are important to maintaining the continued reliability of the drinking water system. Part of the system being upgraded dates back to 1910. These upgrades also improve the resilience of the system to climate change - an important consideration on an offshore island where the geography constrains and limits backup options for supplying the community with water.
I urge the Committee to support LD 2234, increase the borrowing amount for the water district, and help the community implement important infrastructure projects.
10061852:
LD 2234, An Act to Increase the Debt Limit of the Vinalhaven Water District Tes mony of Pamela Alley, Vinalhaven Water District Chairperson Trustee March 19, 2026 @ 1PM
Good afternoon, Chair Sachs and Honorable Members of the Energy, Utilities and Technology Committee:
My name is Pam Alley, and I have served as Chairperson and Trustee of the Vinalhaven Water District for the past 22 years. I appreciate the opportunity to provide testimony in support of LD 2234, "An Act to Increase the Debt Limit of the Vinalhaven Water District."
The district's current debt limit, established in its charter, is $1.5 million. As you can appreciate, this amount does not carry the same purchasing power today as it did when the limit was set in 1978. This constraint has become increasingly challenging as the district works to address critical infrastructure needs and ensure the continued reliability of our island community's drinking water system.
At present, the district is preparing to finalize funding for two significant capital projects. The first is a coordinated effort with the Town of Vinalhaven to support downtown infrastructure improvements and enhance climate-related resiliency. As part of this project, the district will replace approximately 330 linear feet of 10-inch water main that dates back to 1908.
The second project is focused on improving water quality. The district plans to install granular activated carbon vessels to remove organic compounds from the drinking water, thereby meeting and strengthening compliance and improving overall water quality for our customers.
Both projects have received support through the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund, including principal forgiveness and American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) grant funding. Timely execution of this funding is essential to ensure the district does not lose access to these critical funding opportunities. Additionally, operating at or near our existing debt limit leaves the district with minimal flexibility to respond to unforeseen needs, such as emergency repairs or future capital improvements.
As the District evaluated the financial requirements associated with these projects, it became clear that the current debt limit is no longer adequate. For this reason, I respectfully request your support for increasing the Vinalhaven Water District's debt limit from $1.5 million to $4 million. The Board of Trustees and I believe this is a fiscally responsible adjustment that will allow the district to meet necessary infrastructure needs while maintaining prudent financial management.
Thank you for your time and consideration of this legislation. I would be pleased to answer any questions the Committee may have.
